questions.q: Do you find it easy to talk to strangers?
questions.answer: It depends on the setting, but generally yes. I'm fairly comfortable striking up a conversation, and you often learn something interesting. A little friendliness goes a long way in putting people at [[ease]].

questions.q: In what situations do you talk to strangers?
questions.answer: Most often while travelling, on long bus journeys to Dhaka, for instance. Four hours is a long time, so chatting to the person beside you is almost [[inevitable]]. I've had some surprisingly deep conversations that way.

questions.q: Were you told not to talk to strangers as a child?
questions.answer: Yes, my mother was quite strict about it, especially in crowded places like markets. Looking back, it was a [[perfectly reasonable]] rule, although in our small neighbourhood almost nobody was really a stranger.

questions.q: Are people in your country friendly towards strangers?
questions.answer: Generally, very. Bangladeshis are known for their [[warmth]], and it's quite normal for someone to invite a traveller for tea or walk them somewhere rather than just pointing. Foreign visitors often mention how welcoming people are.

questions.q: Do you think it's safe to talk to strangers online?
questions.answer: It can be, but you have to be cautious. It's very easy for people to [[misrepresent themselves]] online, so I'd never share personal details with someone I hadn't met. Young people especially need to be careful.
